text: Philip Rubin is a prominent figure in speech technology and cognitive science, known for his foundational work in articulatory synthesis, speech perception, and sinewave synthesis. He developed key computational models such as ASY and SWS, which advanced the understanding of speech production and perception, and contributed to the development of the HADES signal processing system and the SPIEL programming language. Rubin has held significant leadership roles in science policy and advocacy, including serving as Director of the Division of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation, Assistant Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, and President of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS). He is also recognized for his contributions to ethical issues in research, particularly in human subjects protections and the oversight of emerging technologies. His work has influenced both scientific research and public policy, with a strong focus on embodied cognition and the application of dynamic systems theory to speech and language. Rubin has been honored with numerous fellowships and awards, including from the Acoustical Society of America, the American Psychological Association, and the National Academy of Public Administration. He is a co-founder of Haskins Laboratories' P-01 program and the Auditory-Visual Speech Association (AVISA), and has contributed to public engagement through educational initiatives and advocacy for open science.
